11.title: Await a Result: consume an async function
11.description: The provided `loadLessonTitle()` returns a promise for the string `Grid foundations`. Implement `showLessonTitle()` so it awaits that result and returns the title.
11.learningObjective: Use await inside an async function to read the resolved value from a promise-returning helper.
instructions: Declare showLessonTitle as an async function.
Await the result of loadLessonTitle.
Return the resolved title.
Call showLessonTitle and handle its promise in the sample.

workedExample.explanation: Await pauses only the surrounding async function until the promise settles. It does not block the browser’s main thread.

11.hint: Calling an async function returns a promise; await unwraps its fulfillment value inside another async function.
11.explanation: Await pauses only the surrounding async function until the promise settles. It does not block the browser’s main thread.

testCases.description: Declare an async function.
Use await with loadLessonTitle().
Return the resolved string.
Do not return the unresolved promise as the title.

11.expectedOutput:

Await a Result: consume an async function

Input: await loadLessonTitle()

Expected value: "Grid foundations"

Await pauses only the surrounding async function until the promise settles. It does not block the browser’s main thread.

12.title: Handle a Failed Request: catch async errors
12.description: Implement `loadNotice()` to await the supplied `loadNoticeText()` helper. If it rejects, return `Notice unavailable` so the caller receives a readable result instead of an unhandled rejection.
12.learningObjective: Catch a rejected promise at the user-facing boundary and return a clear fallback message.
instructions: Make loadNotice an async function.
Await loadNoticeText inside a try block.
Catch the rejection and return the requested fallback.
Do not hide a successful message behind the fallback.

workedExample.explanation: Handling an error at the boundary where a fallback is possible keeps expected failures understandable. Avoid swallowing unrelated errors silently in larger systems.

12.hint: A try/catch around await catches a rejection as an exception at that point.
12.explanation: Handling an error at the boundary where a fallback is possible keeps expected failures understandable. Avoid swallowing unrelated errors silently in larger systems.

testCases.description: Await loadNoticeText() inside try.
Return the resolved message on success.
Catch a rejection.
Return Notice unavailable after failure.

12.expectedOutput:
REFERENCE EXAMPLE · NOT A PROGRAM RUN

Handle a Failed Request: catch async errors

Input: loadNoticeText() rejects with Error("offline")

Expected value: "Notice unavailable"

Handling an error at the boundary where a fallback is possible keeps expected failures understandable. Avoid swallowing unrelated errors silently in larger systems.
12.expectedOutputHint: Reference example only — input: loadNoticeText() rejects with Error("offline"); expected value: "Notice unavailable". Submitted code is not executed in this mode.

13.title: Load Independent Panels: run requests together
13.description: The course overview and streak card load independently. Implement `loadDashboard()` to await both helper promises with Promise.all and return an object containing `overview` and `streak`.
13.learningObjective: Use Promise.all to start independent asynchronous operations together and collect their results in order.
instructions: Call both helpers before awaiting their shared result.
Pass both promises to Promise.all.
Destructure the results in the same order.
Return an object with the requested property names.

workedExample.explanation: Parallelizing independent requests can reduce total wait time. Promise.all rejects if any member rejects, so choose it when all results are required.

13.hint: Promise.all preserves the input order of its results even when the operations finish in a different order.
13.explanation: Parallelizing independent requests can reduce total wait time. Promise.all rejects if any member rejects, so choose it when all results are required.

testCases.description: Use Promise.all with both helper calls.

Return the named object properties.

14.title: Keep Partial Results: use allSettled
14.description: Load a course card and a streak card independently. Implement `loadPanels()` to return both settled outcomes so the interface can display whichever panel succeeds.
14.learningObjective: Use Promise.allSettled when independent panel results should be inspected even if one request fails.
instructions: Pass both helper promises to Promise.allSettled.
Await the combined promise.
Return the ordered settled result array.
Do not convert a rejected result into a fulfilled value.

workedExample.explanation: allSettled is useful when partial results are meaningful. The caller still needs to inspect statuses before reading a value.

14.hint: Unlike Promise.all, Promise.allSettled fulfills after every input settles and reports each status.
14.explanation: allSettled is useful when partial results are meaningful. The caller still needs to inspect statuses before reading a value.

15.title: Finish Loading State: reset in finally
15.description: Implement `refreshLessons()` so it sets `state.loading` to true, awaits `loadLessons()`, stores successful lessons, and always resets loading to false in finally.
15.learningObjective: Use finally to clean up a loading flag after either successful or failed asynchronous work.
instructions: Set loading to true before starting the request.
Await loadLessons inside try.
Store the successful lesson list.
Reset loading to false in finally.

workedExample.output: state.loading is false after either outcome
workedExample.explanation: Cleanup belongs in finally when it must occur on both success and failure. The error should still propagate unless the task explicitly handles it.

15.hint: A finally block runs after the try path whether it fulfilled or threw.
15.explanation: Cleanup belongs in finally when it must occur on both success and failure. The error should still propagate unless the task explicitly handles it.
